paper.title: Strong enhancement of Penning ionisation in cold Rydberg gases II: Tom and Jerry pairs for alkali-metal atoms
paper.journal: Journal of Physics B: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics

research.topic: Penning ionisation (PI) in cold Rydberg gases of alkali-metal atoms, focusing on asymmetric pairs (Tom and Jerry pairs) and the influence of quantum defects and Förster resonances.
goals: Systematic investigation of PI for alkali-metal atoms (Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs) excited to high Rydberg states.
Identify optimal asymmetric pairs (Tom and Jerry) that maximize PI width.
Analyze dependence on orbital quantum numbers l and quantum defects.
Examine the role of Förster resonances in enhancing PI efficiency.
methods: Analytical formulas for PI widths and optimal quantum numbers.

states.Tom_Jerry_pairs: Asymmetric pairs with ni >> n_d^(opt), where n_d^(opt) is the optimal principal quantum number of the de-exciting atom (Jerry) for a given ionizing atom (Tom) with principal quantum number ni.

theory.framework: Semiclassical approximation within the Smirnov–Katsuura model for Penning ionisation via dipole–dipole interaction.
key_assumptions: Internuclear distance R exceeds characteristic size of Rydberg states (~n*^2), preventing wavefunction overlap.
Rydberg atoms randomly located, homogeneous population over Zeeman sublevels (no alignment/orientation).
Frozen interatomic distances during observation times (ultracold conditions).
theory.dipole_matrix_element: (N_d' || D || N_d)^2 = l_max [R_{n'l'}^{nl}]^2, l_max = max(l, l') (Eq. 7).
theory.Förster_resonances: Occur when quantum defect difference Δμ_d = μ_{l_d'} - μ_{l_d} is half-integer, leading to up to 5× increase in PI efficiency.

numerical.method: Improved unified semiclassical representation of radial integrals (Appendix A).

parameters.ni_range: Up to 100 (e.g., ni=50 fixed in Fig. 3, Fig. 4 shows ni dependence).
parameters.internuclear_distance: R ≃ 0.56 μm (corresponding to number density ρ_r = 9.9×10^11 cm^{-3}) for physical units in Fig. 3.

calculations: Reduced width ˜Γ_N = R^6 Γ_N as function of nd, ni (Fig. 2).
˜Γ_N vs nd for fixed ni=50 for various species and configurations (Fig. 3).
Optimal n_d^(opt) and peak widths ˜Γ^(opt) vs ni (Fig. 4).

Penning_autoionisation_width.description: Total PI rate constant for a pair of Rydberg atoms at fixed internuclear distance R.

reduced_width.description: R^6 Γ_N, independent of R for dipole–dipole interaction.

gain_coefficient.description: Enhancement factor of PI rate for optimal asymmetric pair vs symmetric pair.

optimal_quantum_number.description: Principal quantum number of de-exciting atom that maximizes PI width for given ni.

photoionisation_cross_section.description: Cross-section for bound-free transition of ionizing atom.

dipole_matrix_element.description: Reduced dipole matrix element for de-exciting atom transition.

key_findings: Optimal asymmetric (Tom and Jerry) pairs show several orders of magnitude increase in PI rate compared to symmetric pairs.
For alkali-metal atoms, PI width strongly depends on orbital quantum numbers l due to quantum defects, unlike hydrogen.
Two PI channels exist for ld > 0 (Δl = ±1), leading to doublet-like optimal pairs.
Förster resonances (half-integer quantum defect difference) enhance PI efficiency up to 5 times.
Gain Λ(ni) for alkali atoms significantly exceeds hydrogen; for ni=50, Λ ranges from 158 (Li) to 482 (Rb) vs 52.4 for H.

optimal_pairs.s_s_pairs: Table 2 gives n_d^(opt) for ni=50: H=17, Li=15, Na=14, K=15, Rb=16, Cs=17.
optimal_pairs.s_p_pairs: Higher reduced widths than s-s pairs due to enhanced dipole moment for short bound-bound transitions (ld=0 → l_d'=1).
optimal_pairs.doublet_structure: For ld > 0, two distinct optimal pairs corresponding to l_d' = ld ± 1.

results.Förster_resonance_effect: When Δμ_d = half-integer, PI efficiency increases up to 5 times. This occurs for certain alkali species and l-configurations.

Fig_1.description: Schematic representation of Auger-like Penning ionisation process: resonance coupling of Rydberg pair A_D^**, A_I^** to continuum. Shows dipole transitions ld, li → l_d', l_i', target levels indexed by κ, energy ω_dd' = ω_dd',κ, free electron energy ε_i',κ = ω_dd',κ - ε_0i.
Fig_1.content: Energy level diagram with initial states, virtual threshold n_th', and final states.

Fig_2.description: Reduced width ˜Γ_N as grey scale map vs nd, ni for Li atoms: (a) s–s (ld=0, li=0), (b) s–p (ld=0, li=1). Shows significant increase in s–p configuration. Oscillatory structure (ridges and valleys) visible.

Fig_3.description: ˜Γ_N for ni=50 vs nd for various species and configurations: s–p Li (red solid), s–s Li (black solid), Na (black dashed), K (green solid), H (blue dashed/dotted). Right axis shows Γ_N in s^{-1} for R=0.56 μm, ρ_r=9.9×10^11 cm^{-3}. Highlights dramatic dependence on orbital configuration and oscillatory trend.
Fig_3.content: Line plots of reduced width and physical PI width.

Fig_4.description: (a) Optimal n_d^(opt) vs ni for s–s pairs of alkali atoms. (b) Reduced widths ˜Γ^(opt) (optimal) and ˜Γ^(sym) (symmetric) vs ni. Gain Λ reaches ~2×10^3 near ni=100.
Fig_4.content: Plots of optimal quantum number and widths vs ni.

equations.Eq_1: PI reaction: A_I^** (n_i, l_i) + A_D^** (n_d, l_d) → A_I^+ + e(p_i', l_i') + A_D^** (n_d', l_d')
equations.Eq_2: Hydrogen scaling: n_d^(opt) ≃ 2^{1/3} n_i^{2/3}, Γ^(opt) ≃ n_i Γ^(sym)
equations.Eq_5: Total PI rate: Γ_N = (1/R^6) Σ_{α} ˜Γ_N^{(α)}; ˜Γ_N^{(α)} = Σ_{β} Σ_{n_d'} c σ_ph(p_i') / (π ω_dd') * (N_d' || D || N_d)^2 / (2l_d+1)
equations.Eq_6: Radial integral: R_{n'l'}^{nl}(p'l') = ∫ R_{nl}(r) R_{n'l'}(p'l')(r) r^3 dr
equations.Eq_7: Dipole matrix element: (N_d' || D || N_d)^2 = l_max [R_{n'l'}^{nl}]^2, l_max = max(l, l')
equations.Eq_B12_B13: Analytical description of oscillatory nature of ˜Γ_N (Appendix B.1).

model_limitations: Semiclassical approximation accuracy ~17% for aggregate PI widths.
Assumes frozen interatomic distances (ultracold limit); thermal motion not included (though formula for thermal PI cross-section σ_PI = 5.00 ˜Γ_N^{2/5} v^{-2/5} is mentioned).
Random spatial distribution and homogeneous Zeeman population assumed.
Quantum defects taken from literature (Table 1); may have uncertainties for high n.
scope_limitations: Focus on alkali-metal atoms; hydrogen used for comparison.
Only dipole–dipole interaction considered; higher multipoles neglected.
PI channels limited to Δl = ±1 for both atoms.

cited_in_text.context: Previous paper on Tom and Jerry pairs for hydrogen atoms (Efimov et al 2016 J. Phys. B: At. Mol. Opt. Phys. 49 125302).
